claims.text: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation processing can simultaneously improve yield strength and tensile ductility in a room-temperature-brittle refractory multi-principal-element alloy.
The demonstrated starting alloy has a supersaturated matrix and a dual bcc/fcc phase structure.
Refractory high-entropy alloys commonly have poor room-temperature tensile ductility because brittle secondary phases such as B2, silicides, or Laves phases form.
Heavy cold rolling sharply increases dislocation density and produces high-density dislocation walls.
Annealing at 900 °C produces coherent D0a δ nano-lamellae and leads to recrystallization of ultrafine fcc grains.
The stated 900 °C annealing treatment sequentially produces both δ-lamellae and D022 γ″ particles.
A subsequent aging treatment at 650 °C is required in the cited system to form the high-density D022 γ″ particles.
Controlling the Ni/Fe ratio between 2 and 4 suppresses formation of the topologically close-packed μ phase at phase boundaries.
Adding 5 at.% Ta creates a supersaturated solid solution suitable for precipitation of Ni3Ta-based δ and γ″ phases.
The processed alloy contains coherent δ-lamellae and γ″ particles within an fcc matrix.
Dislocations shear through the coherent δ-lamellae and form slip bands without initiating cracks at strains up to 14%.
γ″ particles pin dislocations while the δ-lamellae permit dislocation transmission.
The dual coherent precipitation structure relieves local stress concentrations and promotes progressive strain hardening.
Coherent interfaces prevent interfacial decohesion while supplying precipitation strengthening.
The processed tungsten-based refractory HEA can attain ambient-temperature strength above 2 GPa together with about 15% tensile ductility.
The processed alloy can retain yield strength above 1 GPa at 800 °C.
Conventional thermal treatments or single-principal-element designs cannot achieve comparable strength-ductility synergy.
The strategy is applicable to other refractory high-entropy alloys whenever coherent precipitation is thermodynamically feasible and brittle intermetallic phases can be suppressed.
The strategy will not be effective when precipitates are inherently incoherent or the matrix remains intrinsically brittle regardless of microstructure.
The long-term stability of the coherent precipitates under cyclic loading remains unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The stated route specifies cold rolling followed by annealing at 900 °C for 1 hour, yet it expects a dual δ/γ″ structure. The cited evidence states that 900 °C annealing forms δ-lamellae, whereas γ″ particles form only during a subsequent 650 °C aging step, which is omitted from the stated conditions.
